The PEAKS Act highlights a critical problem: rural hospitals hemorrhaging cash while D.C. plays accounting games. Medicare’s reimbursement rules for CAH ambulances in mountainous areas are textbook bureaucratic insanity—forcing providers to meet a 35-mile radius requirement despite terrain making 15 miles functionally impassable. Fixing this misalignment is necessary, but slapping a temporary payment parity patch (FY2025 extensions) without structural reform just kicks the can.

Rural CAHs have seen operating margins plummet 8% since 2019, yet Congress offers Band-Aid bills instead of overhauling Medicare’s broken payment models. This bill’s $15 million price tag is a rounding error compared to the $100B+ wasted annually on hospital administrative bloat, but it’s still taxpayer money propping up a system that rewards inefficiency.

Bipartisan support? Predictable. Both parties love funding rural healthcare theater while ignoring systemic rot.
